A.note: Tight, correct schema with composite same-org FKs, a query-keyed index table, and an access query that also handles public/internal visibility in SQL.

errors: Calls every access-check branch 'index-only or close to it'; most branches need heap fetches for permission/role, a loose claim rather than a bug
B.note: Solid and correct with good polymorphic-vs-two-tables reasoning and a sensible denormalisation trigger, but visibility is left to the app and adds little beyond A.

C.note: Invariants listed up front and enforced in schema, org base permission, a correct FOR UPDATE last-admin guard and targeted tests; somewhat longer than the question needs.

errors: granted_by REFERENCES users(id) with no ON DELETE action, so deleting any user who ever granted access fails with an FK violation
team_memberships has no org_id or FK to org_memberships, so a non-member can be put on a team and removal from the org relies on application code to clean up team memberships
Permission ladder reduced to read/write/admin (simplification, not stated as a trade-off)
D.note: The effective-access view is a clean single entry point, but the schema drops the team-member-is-org-member constraint and has a user-delete-blocking FK.

E.note: Each index is tied to a numbered query, ON DELETE choices are explained, the last-admin race is closed by locking the org row, and the tests are concrete.

F.note: Correct and well argued, with the list-column rejection stated explicitly and a full index-to-query table; the feature table and index list repeat each other a little.
